summary: F-M3-2 is fixed by a general post-animation pass (bodyClearance.ts): after the animator and pose blend, key bones (Head, Neck, Spine2, Hips, shoulders, hands) are measured against every nearby non-ground solid at its true size and the visual root is pushed horizontally away (instant in, smooth release, max 1 m); physics, capsule and camera are untouched and nothing moves in the open. Lab wall crouch head clearance went from 0.07 m (0.19 m inside the wall in the before screenshot) to 0.17 m, wall tests pass, and the open-ground hard landing is visually and numerically unchanged.

criteria.criterion: F-M3-2 is fixed by a general mechanism, not a per-wall standoff tweak (for example choosing the soft landing or limiting forward lean when a wall is close in front, or keeping the visual body inside the capsule's clear space), so that in every clip and blend (idle, walk, run, jump, fall, land, and their transitions) the head, neck, chest and hips bones stay at least 0.05 m outside every non-ground collider; the landing still looks natural in the open.
criteria.evidence: components/game/bodyClearance.ts runs last in the frame driver (after animator and pose blend, via GameScene.tsx and GameAvatar.tsx) for every clip and blend. It measures 8 key bones against every nearby non-ground solid at true size (oriented boxes, no standoff) and pushes the visual root horizontally to a per-bone margin of at least bone radius + 0.05 m; no per-wall or per-clip values. Test drives idle, walk, run, jump, fall, land and transitions at every face. Open ground: no solid near, no push (test asserts maxPush 0) and the screenshots are unchanged.

criteria.criterion: An automated test drives real physics and the real animator on the campus: for every wall face generated from the layout (at least 20, including lab-side-l, lab-side-r, lab-back and the tower wings), the avatar jumps and lands pressed against the wall facing it, diagonally and sideways, and per-frame bone clearance never drops below 0.05 m for head, neck, chest and hips; the test fails on the current code and passes after.

assumptions: The 0.17 m minimum for Head in the browser sampler is the pass's own margin for that bone (bone radius plus 0.05 m) measured to the true surface, so the 0.05 m acceptance bound holds with room.

Some hedge wall runs only produced soft landings (crouchMinHeadRel 1.03), so the hard-landing crouch at walls is proven by the physics test hard-drop mode and by the before/after Lab wall screenshots rather than by every browser run.

The open-ground hard landing was driven by a run across the three terraces and off the top (impact above the 6.5 m/s threshold, crouchMinHeadRel 0.64 to 0.65) because that is the only 2.4 m drop outside the buildings.
decisionsProposed: Keep the body-clearance pass as the single mechanism that keeps the visible avatar out of level geometry; new clips or poses need no per-wall tuning, and the test in bodyClearance.test.ts enumerates every wall face from the layout.
lessonsProposed: Animation poses move bones far off the capsule axis (hard-landing crouch puts the head 0.5 m ahead), so a capsule standoff alone never guarantees visual clearance; measure bone-to-solid distance on the finished pose.

When driving the avatar up the terrace in a browser harness, jump at 0.9 to 1.0 m run-up before each face with Shift held; walking or jumping against the face leaves the capsule hovering on the corner.
A cut-off stage leaves valuable scratch results; verify them against the current tree timestamps before reusing instead of redoing.
